## What the two commands actually establish

`crimes verdict --format json` (run from the fixture; git root resolved to the tracked mirror at `examples/messy-ts-app`, same 42 findings):

```
verdict: "unchanged"   new: 0   fixed: 0   unchanged: 42
reasons: ["no new findings and no fixed findings"]
recommended_actions: ["no maintainability change vs. base — verdict is advisory only."]
```

**Nothing here is a regression.** All 42 are pre-existing debt against `origin/main`, so no finding is a merge blocker and the plan below is paydown sequencing, not gate-clearing. Order by value, not by fear.

Two things to know before reading the list:

1. **The "top 10" is an agent-risk ranking, not a severity ranking.** The findings arrive sorted by `scores.agent_risk` (0.44 → 0.36). That's the right default for "what will an agent misread", but it demotes the biggest structural crimes: `generateInvoice` (204 lines, `severity 0.9`) sits at **#36** on `agent_risk 0.11`, and God File `src/billing.ts` at **#39**. I flag both below rather than pretending the cut-off is meaningful.
2. **Three of the six scores are dead in this repo.** Every one of the 42 findings has `churn: 0`, `recency: 0`, and `blast_radius: 0` — no git history and no importer graph feeding the scan. The ranking is running on `severity`, `confidence`, `agent_risk`, and `test_gap` only. That directly empties one of your requested buckets.

---

## Triage order

I've collapsed the 10 into 5 work units, because 5 of them pair up into single changes.

### 1. Contract Split-Brain — `src/api/state.ts` ↔ `src/billing.ts` · **fix now**
`crime_00010` (User, sev 0.90) + `crime_00011` (Invoice, sev **0.96**)

Highest severity in the whole report, and one fix. `Invoice` disagrees on six fields, five of them money/identity: `subtotalCents`, `taxCents`, `discountCents`, `currency`, `userId`, `createdAt` — all declared in `billing.ts:19`, all absent from `state.ts:9`. Evidence: *"Nothing in the build checks the two declarations against each other."* An agent reading `state.ts` will write correct-looking code that silently drops tax.

`crime_00011` ranks **#11** — one slot outside your top 10 — purely because `agent_risk` ties at 0.36. Do not split them. This unit is also a **prerequisite**: don't touch `generateInvoice` until `Invoice` has one declaration.

### 2. `src/date.ts` time-domain cluster · **fix now**
`crime_00001` (Temporal Recklessness, ar **0.44** — highest in the report) + `crime_00009` (Half-UTC/Half-Local, sev 0.80)

Six of the 42 findings live in this one file (also `00013` unzoned parse, `00019` DST-naive `+86400000`, `00029` string-sewing, `00030` locale drift). They are all one missing abstraction. The deciding detail is in `00001`'s evidence: *"1 decide a branch or comparison (lines 4)"* — that reading changes behaviour, not just output. Contrast `crime_00014` (billing.ts, 7 reads, *"none decide a branch"*), which is why it correctly ranks lower.

Sequence inside the unit: inject the clock first, *then* unify on UTC — reversing it means rewriting the same lines twice.

### 3. Missing Agent Context · **fix now** (do it today, in parallel)
`crime_00003`

The cheapest agent-risk reduction available and zero code risk: no `AGENTS.md`, no `CLAUDE.md`, no `SKILL.md`, and `package.json` declares a `bin` (`messy`) that nothing documents. It's the only finding that lowers the risk of every *other* fix on this list, so it shouldn't queue behind them.

One caveat: it's attributed to `src/api/files.ts`, but it's a repo-level finding pinned to an arbitrary file. Don't read it as a `files.ts` problem.

### 4. `/settings/billing` identity · **fix now**
`crime_00005` (Duplicated Navigation Source) + `crime_00006` (Route Metadata Drift)

One destination described four ways — component `PricingPage`, `metadata.title` "Plans", `<title>` "Subscription", nav labels "Plans" *and* "Billing". Two detectors, one bug, one change. Low risk, and it's the classic case where an agent updates one label and leaves three stale.

### 5. `"enterprise"` literal scatter · **fix now** (constant only)
`crime_00004`

Four production files across four layers (`api`, `billing`, `jobs`, `ui`). Worth reading alongside two findings further down: `crime_00016` puts the actual rule in prose only (*"Only owners can refund enterprise plans unless billing support approves"*), and `crime_00028` is a test literally named *"renders the enterprise plan"* with **zero** assertions. So the enterprise concept currently has scattered literals, an unencoded rule, and a test that proves nothing.

Extract the constant now (`suggested_actions` risk: medium — it touches four areas). Consolidating the *policy* is a separate, larger piece of work.

## Three things the top 10 hides

**`src/billing.ts` is the real hotspot, and no single finding says so.** It carries eight findings directly (`00014`, `00015`, `00016`, `00021`, `00032`, `00036`, `00039`, `00042`) and is the counterpart file in `00004`, `00010`, and `00011` — roughly a quarter of the report. Ranked by `agent_risk`, its worst offender lands at #36. With `churn` live, this file would have surfaced on its own.

**`crime_00018` is broken right now and ranks #18.** `/Users/andrew/dev/crimes/schema.json` hardcoded at `files.ts:9`, next to `localhost:3000` at L8 (`00017`) and the three sync calls at L12–15 (`00007`) — all inside the same ~10-line `loadPlanSchema`. That path fails on every other machine and every CI runner. Effort is `quick`. I'd promote the whole 10-line function to **fix now** as one cleanup, ahead of unit 5, despite two of its three findings sitting outside the top 10.

**Don't let an agent split `generateInvoice` as a drive-by.** It's 204 lines, 3.4× threshold, and it contains a swallowed error (`00032`: *"the catch declares no binding"*) and a misleadingly-named `calculateRefundPreview` that sends email (`00015`). It needs the refactor, but per the auto-fix policy that's a proposed, approved change — and only *after* unit 1 lands, since it's the code that consumes the split-brained `Invoice`.

One scan caveat worth carrying: coverage warns that 1 file (`.crimes/suppressions.json`) matched an exclude and was never read — *"findings in it are absent, not zero."* Immaterial here, but it means 42 is a floor, not a total.
